To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new site amplification model is developed for crustal earthquakes, which includes the deep soil effects and is based on a global dataset, and the model is applicable in the entire world.

(a) The nonlinear site amplification is formulated in terms input rock motion and site stiffness, (b) the soil nonlinearity can be described by a sigmoid function, (c) the soil stiffness is a function of shear wave velocity at the depth of 30 m (V30), (d) the site-variability decreases with decreasing V30 or increasing input motion, (e) the site variability can be represented by a period average of 0.43 for a given input
the site nonlinearity is a function of soil stiffness and input rock motion and the deep soil effect is a function of the soil stiffness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new nonlinear site model for crustal events and its applications in probabilistic seismic hazard analysis.
the development and application of a new site model which is capable of describing the site-variability of strong ground motions in terms of input motion, soil stiffness and deep soil effect.
the development of a new nonlinear site amplification model for global crustal earthquakes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the developed model is capable of representing the nonlinear site amplification for crustal earthquakes in a global scale.
the site model developed in this research is able to predict the site response in a wide range of input motions and soil conditions.
this model is a robust tool for estimating the nonlinear site amplification of crustal earthquakes for a broad range of input motions, soil conditions and earthquake magnitudes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed model provides a simple, robust and accurate method for nonlinear site amplification.
the proposed site model provides an efficient and practical tool for the site amplification of crustal earthquakes.
a simple and practical site model for crustal earthquake is developed which can be used in seismic hazard analysis.

the site model can be easily used in seismic hazard analyses.
the nonlinear site effects can be modeled with the input motion at rock site condition and soil stiffness.
